name: Parallax Zoom Deep-Dive
summary: Slide advances fly the camera FORWARD into the scene instead of sliding sideways: foreground planes separate and rush past while distant layers hold, so every transition reads as a dolly-through — traveling deeper into the world rather than turning a page.

composition: Full-bleed immersive scene with a centered dominant headline stack; the scene does the work around the type.
Foreground silhouettes (cliffs, arches, portals) frame the composition like a natural vignette AND give the zoom something to rush past — the transition is only as good as the foreground occluders.
A slide counter and minimal arrows acknowledge the sequence without breaking immersion.
layering: Explicit multi-plane depth (near silhouettes → mid haze → far field) built BEFORE the transition: idle cursor-parallax proves the depth that the zoom then exploits.
On advance, the outgoing scene scales up past the camera while the incoming scene resolves from a deeper zoom — two scenes exist simultaneously mid-flight.
The headline floats on the frontmost plane and restages per scene.
lighting: A glowing scene core (nebula, portal light) acts as a backlight behind the headline, giving type a halo.
Warm center bloom + darkened cool edges = a natural vignette that funnels the eye and hides plane seams during the zoom.
typography: Editorial pairing: small italic script accent above a colossal slab/serif display — a travel-poster cadence.
Type staggers in per scene (script leads, slab follows, CTA last) then holds still while the scene breathes.

rules: Deep dark base tinted warm per scene; one luminous accent reserved for the display type and active UI.
Cool-dark shadows anchor warm midtones — the warm/cool split is what makes the depth read at night.

easing: Long ease-in-out on the zoom with a slight settle at arrival; parallax layers use expo-out damping to rest.
No linearity — a linear zoom reads as a scale tween, not a camera move.
pacing: Slow, ~1s+ per transition; the dive is the spectacle, so it earns real duration.
Idle scenes keep gentle cursor parallax so depth never disappears between transitions.
choreography: Transition order: camera pushes → outgoing foreground rushes past and fades → incoming scene resolves from depth → type restages.
Swipe/drag direction can map to dive depth for a tactile feel.

gapNotes: The fly-through primitive and hub transition presets exist, but a zoom-THROUGH transition that holds two layered scenes simultaneously mid-flight is not among the shipped presets (curtain/veil/dissolve/wipe/glass-sweep) — needs a new preset.
Depth-plane scene assembly from generated imagery (cutout + depth) is the W-PHOTO R2 pipeline.
Center-bloom + edge-vignette grading needs the R1 cinematic floor post stack.

whenToUse: World-building narratives: travel, games, cosmic/nature themes, chaptered storytelling where each slide is a place.
As the signature transition for a hub whose content is a journey.
whenNotToUse: Utilitarian, data-dense, or fast-task UIs — slow cinematic zooms cost patience.
Scenes without strong foreground occluders — the dive reads as a plain scale-up.
Motion-sensitive audiences: forward zoom is the most vestibularly aggressive transition; must honor reduced-motion with a crossfade.

notes: Builds directly on layered-photo-parallax-hero: the idle parallax establishes the depth model the zoom transition then travels through.
Clashes with grid/dashboard families — the dive assumes one immersive scene per state.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as seasonal-theme-shift — both are whole-scene state changes; offer one scene-morph family per set.

sources.title: Starry Night Parallax Zoom Slider
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: all 4 slides advanced via swipe/drag in both directions; forward-dive transitions observed with foreground cliffs rushing past; idle cursor-move parallax verified plane separation before each dive.

exemplars.promptSummary: Layered deep-space scene: near rocky arch framing a mid nebula and far starfield, warm-core/cool-edge light — the dolly-through depth stack.
